title: The signal
subtitle: Why I started coding
body: Computer science was the first subject where I could build, not just memorize. In classes 11 and 12, that hands-on process pulled me in completely, and by the end I knew what I wanted: to make things, not just study them.

title: A beginning, not an end
subtitle: The first hackathon
body: My first hackathon ended in a project that didn't work the way we planned. It taught me more than any course could: that shipping something imperfect beats not shipping at all. That failure became the starting point for everything after it.

title: Learning to speak
subtitle: The stage
body: For a long time I stayed quiet in rooms full of people. The first time I walked on stage to introduce myself, unprepared and unsure, changed that. It's a habit I'm still building, one event at a time.

title: Eight minutes
subtitle: Budget Lens
body: At Budget Lens, an eight-minute presentation and a sharper Q&A round earned us first prize. It was proof that preparation and a clear point of view can hold up under pressure.

title: What drives me
subtitle: The story so far
body: I'm drawn to building things that work, learning in public, and helping the people a step behind me. I don't have it all figured out, and I don't think anyone does at nineteen. But I'd rather try and adjust than wait for certainty.
